title: Normalization of weighted forms
statement: Let $I$ be a finite set, let $w_i,p,\rho\in\mathbb{R}$ with $p\ne0$, and let $f:I\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfy $G(f)>0$, where $G(h)=\sum_iw_i|h_i|^p$ and $F(h)=\rho^2\sum_iw_i h_i^2+(1-\rho^2)(\sum_iw_i h_i)^2$. Set $c=G(f)^{-1/p}$. Then $G(cf)=1$ and $F(cf)=F(f)/G(f)^{2/p}$.
replaced: Let $I$ be finite, $w:I\to\bbr$, $p\ne0$, and $\rho\in\bbr$. Define $G(f)=\sum_iw_i|f_i|^p$ and $F(f)=\rho^2\sum_iw_if_i^2+(1-\rho^2)(\sum_iw_if_i)^2$. If $G(f)>0$ and $c=G(f)^{-1/p}$, then $G(cf)=1$ and $F(cf)=F(f)/G(f)^{2/p}$.
